record.context_brief: Pure point spectrum with non-short-range nonlinearity
record.original_question: Consider a Hamiltonian system whose linearized operator, for example -Delta_f + v, has pure point spectrum, with part of that pure point spectrum dense in some finite interval. If the nonlinear part of the Hamiltonian is not short range, as in Hamiltonian partial differential equations posed on the whole space, do KAM tori still exist for that system?

evidence.quote: Here is no any conditions imposed on the normal frequencies lambda_n's, except that which are of pure point spectra and are non-zero. Therefore, these frequencies can densely distributed on an finite interval. For example, they can be all rational number in the interval [1,2].

Problem 2. Assume that the linearized operator (-Delta_f +v, for example,) of a hamiltonian system is of pure point spectra, part of which is dense in some finite interval, and assume that the nonlinear part of the Hamiltonian is not of short rang (in partial differential equations defined in the whole space, for example). Are there any KAM tori for the system? This problem is apparently open.

artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal an extensive literature on KAM theorems for Hamiltonian PDEs, including results for unbounded perturbations and for the quantum harmonic oscillator (which has pure point spectrum) under spatially localized time quasi-periodic perturbations. However, the specific configuration combining (i) normal frequencies dense in a finite interval and (ii) a non-short-range (non-localized) nonlinear perturbation on the whole space does not appear to be covered by available KAM theorems, and no resolution of this combined problem was found.

status_evidence.title: Pure Point Spectrum of the Floquet Hamiltonian for the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator Under Time Quasi-Periodic Perturbations
status_evidence.snippet: The 1-d quantum harmonic oscillator is stable under spatially localized, time quasi-periodic perturbations on a set of Diophantine frequencies of positive measure.
status_evidence.claim: Existing KAM-type results for operators with pure point spectrum (harmonic oscillator) require spatially localized (short-range) perturbations.

status_evidence.title: A KAM Theorem for Hamiltonian Partial Differential Equations with Unbounded Perturbations
status_evidence.snippet: An abstract infinite dimensional KAM theorem dealing with unbounded perturbation vector-fields, applicable to a class of Hamiltonian PDEs.
status_evidence.claim: KAM theorems for Hamiltonian PDEs with unbounded perturbations exist, but typical hypotheses do not allow normal frequencies dense in an interval together with non-short-range nonlinearities.
